children.text: Founded by Spain in the 16th century as a trading city, Vigan was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in recognition of having the most intact Spanish colonial townscape in Asia. The cobblestones of Calle Crisologo, kalesa carriages, and Ilocos empanada welcome travelers.

Vigan, the capital of Ilocos Sur in northwestern Luzon, is a historic city sitting at the mouth of the Mestizo River near the South China Sea. After the Spanish conquistador Juan de Salcedo established a base here in

, Vigan flourished as northern Luzon's outpost in the galleon trade network linking Chinese merchants from Fujian with Acapulco, Mexico. The mansions built by the Chinese-mestizo merchant families who grew wealthy from this trade form today's old town.

Vigan's mansions follow a distinctive style called "bahay na bato" (house of stone). The ground floor is built thick with brick and lime, used for storerooms and shops, while the second floor is built of wood with capiz-shell windows and used as living space. Thanks to this blend of Chinese brickwork, Spanish urban planning, and a structure suited to the Philippine tropical climate, UNESCO inscribed Vigan as a World Heritage Site in
as "the best-preserved planned Spanish colonial town in Asia."

Unlike Manila's Intramuros, which was largely destroyed during World War II, Vigan escaped major damage in the war, leaving its old streets almost intact. It was also named one of the "New7Wonders Cities" in
. After sunset, gaslamp-style streetlights illuminate the cobblestones, and the sight of kalesa (horse-drawn carriages) passing by feels as if time has stopped.

The old town has 233 historic buildings lined up along 25 streets laid out in a neat grid, centered on Plaza Salcedo and Plaza Burgos. The Mestizo District, home to Calle Crisologo, is where the Chinese-mestizo merchant families once lived together, and the layout grouping the cathedral, the archbishop's palace, and the provincial capitol around the plazas faithfully reflects the colonial town planning of Spain's Laws of the Indies. The Archbishop's Palace next to the cathedral is the only Spanish-era archbishop's palace remaining in the Philippines and still serves as the residence of the Archbishop of Nueva Segovia. The city has a population of about 54,500 (
); the old town's sights can be explored on foot, and even outlying spots like Baluarte are just
15–20 minutes
away by tricycle.

Vigan is ideal for travelers who love history, architecture, photography, and food, and being a small, walkable city, it works fine for family trips too. Combining it with Laoag and Paoay makes it easy to expand into a loop around the Ilocos region.

Vigan's iconic cobblestone street, lined on both sides with two-story mansions and closed to most vehicle traffic. Enjoy the souvenir shops and cafes by day and the illuminated street atmosphere by night. It's worth walking the same street twice, once in daylight and once at night.
A tour of the town's sights in a horse-drawn carriage. A short
30-minute
loop of the old town costs about
, while a sightseeing circuit out to Baluarte, Pagburnayan, and the Bantay Bell Tower takes
2–3 hours
, with the fare set by negotiation. A kalesa usually seats 3–4 people, so before setting off, confirm the route, the fare, and whether it's per carriage or per person.

blocks.title: St. Paul's Cathedral and the Plaza Salcedo fountain show

children.text: Built
in the "Earthquake Baroque" style, with thick walls and buttresses to withstand earthquakes, the cathedral and the plaza in front of it form the heart of Vigan. The facade cracked in the
earthquake and reinforcement and restoration work is ongoing, so check on site whether the interior is open to visitors. The octagonal bell tower, about
tall and standing separately to the south, was repaired after the earthquake and rings its bells again. At the Plaza Salcedo pond, a free musical fountain show is held daily from

blocks.title: Syquia Mansion and old mansion museums

children.text: Syquia Mansion (built
), once the home of Quirino, the sixth president, and his wife, charges about

admission (discounts for students and seniors) and is closed on Tuesdays. The Crisologo Museum, the former home of the Crisologo family, accepts donations only, while National Museum Ilocos, housed in Father Burgos's birthplace and the old provincial jail, is free and closed on Mondays. Syquia Mansion and the Crisologo Museum close for a lunch break from

This street of workshops, where the traditional Ilocos jar called burnay is made, lies around Liberation Boulevard and Gomez Street on the west side of the old town. You can watch clay being shaped on a potter's wheel and try it yourself; entry and the hands-on experience are free, and you leave a voluntary donation in the box on your way out. Everything from small flowerpots to large jars is for sale on the spot.
About
5–10 minutes
from town by tricycle, this brick bell tower of Bantay Church stands on a hill and once also served as a watchtower against pirate raids. Part of it collapsed in the

earthquake, so you can no longer climb it and access around the tower is restricted, but you can still photograph it from the hillside steps and the surrounding park. Be sure to visit Bantay Church right next to it as well.
Baluarte is a private zoo and park about
15–20 minutes

by car from Calle Crisologo; admission is free, and you can see lions, tigers, giraffes, camels, and a taxidermy exhibit (the Safari Gallery), though activities like animal feeding cost extra. Hidden Garden in Bulala has an Ilocano restaurant set inside a tropical plant garden, making it a good lunch spot.

This orange-colored fried empanada, made from a rice-flour dough filled with shredded green papaya, egg, and Vigan longganisa, is a must on any Vigan trip. Try one dipped in vinegar sauce from a stall at Plaza Burgos.

7–9 hours

Luxury buses (about

The Partas terminal in Vigan is on Alcantara Street in town; take a tricycle from there to your accommodation in the old town.

The old town is easily explored on foot. For sights a little further out, use a tricycle (about
for a short trip in town) or a kalesa.
Vehicle access to Calle Crisologo is restricted, so if your accommodation is on the street itself, you may need to carry your luggage in on foot from the entrance.
The Ilocos region has a clear dry and wet season. In the dry season,
November–May
, rain is rare and walking is pleasant, and
December–February
is relatively cool, good even for midday walking tours.
March–May
is very hot and dry, with midday temperatures sometimes topping
, so plan your schedule around mornings and evenings.
June–October
is the rainy season, affected by the southwest monsoon and typhoons, and northwestern Luzon gets especially heavy rainfall in
July–September
. Notable festivals include the Vigan Longganisa Festival around the city's founding anniversary on
January 22
, and the Viva Vigan Arts Festival in
early May
, filled with street performances and traditional costume parades. Old town accommodation sells out early during Holy Week and year-end, so book ahead.

In Vigan, it's well worth staying at least once in a heritage hotel converted from an old mansion. Calle Crisologo and the surrounding lanes have several centuries-old bahay na bato mansions turned into hotels, impressive for their high ceilings, wooden floors, and antique furniture. Prices run about
per night. If your budget is smaller, a guesthouse on the edge of the old town (about
) works fine too — just pick a spot you can walk to Calle Crisologo from.

Vigan is also one of the Philippines' foremost food cities. Signature dishes include the strongly garlicky, tangy Vigan longganisa, crispy fried pork belly bagnet, the tangy beef-innard soup sinanglao, shrimp fritters okoy, and the Ilocano vegetable stew pinakbet. "Cafe Leona," an old restaurant at the end of Calle Crisologo, has been a landmark for a long time, and the empanada stalls at Plaza Burgos get crowded with locals every evening. Good gifts include Vigan longganisa, the Ilocos vinegar "sukang Iloco," and traditional abel textiles.
Notable places to stay include Villa Angela Heritage House, a 19th-century mansion where Tom Cruise stayed while filming "Born on the Fourth of July" (

), and Hotel Luna, an art hotel displaying Philippine artworks such as Juan Luna's "The Mandolin Player." For empanada, the stalls at Plaza Burgos and the long-running shop Irene's are famous, and Lilong & Lilang (opened
), the restaurant inside Hidden Garden in Bulala, is surrounded by greenery and serves Ilocano home cooking such as bagnet, pinakbet, and sinanglao.
For photos of Calle Crisologo, shoot around
6–7 AM
, when it's nearly empty and you can frame just the cobblestones and mansions.
When taking a kalesa, agree clearly beforehand on whether the fare is per "
1 hour
" or per "route." It's best to avoid a driver who appears to mistreat the horse.
The midday sun is very strong. Bring a parasol or hat and water, and rest at a museum or cafe during the hottest hours.
Downtown Vigan has plenty of ATMs and convenience stores, but street stalls and kalesa only accept cash.
The Plaza Salcedo fountain show usually starts daily at
and runs about
30 minutes
, and on weekends there is sometimes a second show at
. The schedule may change for events, so check locally.
National Museum Ilocos is closed on Mondays and Syquia Mansion on Tuesdays. If you're only in town for one day on a Monday or Tuesday, plan around the closures.
Souvenirs tend to be a bit cheaper at shops one block away from Calle Crisologo.
If you're flying through Laoag Airport, consider combining the trip with Ilocos Norte sights such as Paoay Church (a World Heritage site) and Batac Church.
Tourist maps and announcements of festivals and events can be found on the
official Vigan City website
Calle Crisologo's cobblestones are uneven and slippery when wet. Avoid high heels, and watch your footing at night.
Don't touch the antique furniture and artifacts inside the mansions and museums, and follow any no-photography signs.
Watch out for pickpockets during crowded evening hours and festival periods.
Midday walking tours in
March–May
carry a risk of heatstroke. Drink plenty of water.
Don't agree to touts' "special tours" or excessive kalesa fares, and check the price first.
During the rainy and typhoon season, the northern coastal road can flood and buses can be delayed. In
July 2023
, Typhoon Egay washed away part of the old Quirino (Banaoang) Bridge over the Abra River near Vigan, and in
July 2025
, Typhoon Emong made landfall in Candon, Ilocos Sur. In
July–September
, be sure to check forecasts from PAGASA, the Philippine weather agency.
The magnitude 7.0 Abra earthquake on

toppled part of the Bantay Bell Tower and damaged the walls and windows of Syquia Mansion, St. Paul's Cathedral, and other sites. The cathedral facade has been under scaffolding for reinforcement work since
, and the Bantay Bell Tower still cannot be climbed. Check whether sites are open before you visit.
